page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i1.2xlarge is a member of the Local SSDs instance family, configured with dedicated compute resources and directly attached storage. The instance runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, delivering 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. System memory totals 32.0 GB, providing an even 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 446 GB of local SSD storage, 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and zero integrated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations highlight the constraints of the underlying legacy CPU architecture. In raw computational benchmarks, the ecs.i1.2xlarge scored 952.0 on Geekbench single-core and 3,583.0 on Geekbench multi-core, landing both in the bottom 25% of measured systems. Similarly, stress-ng multi-core reached 5,883.35, placing in the lower quartile. While PassMark CPU composite results fall in the middle tier at 6,992.14, data compression tests show limited efficiency, with single-threaded gzip throughput reaching 18.95 GB/sec. Large uncached memory writes placed in the average tier at 35.61 GB/sec, though overall database and in-memory operations demonstrated weaker output, reflected by 5.89 million Redis SET operations per second.

The presence of 446 GB of local SSD storage offers lower access latency than pure network-attached volumes, but overall compute and memory throughput remain modest compared to contemporary standards. From a resource perspective, the instance trades raw single-thread speed for dedicated execution cores, balanced memory, and direct-attached disk access. It serves best for mid-tier localized relational databases, distributed caching nodes, batch file handling, and internal testing environments requiring direct local scratch space without high CPU overhead.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i1.2xlarge belongs to the Local SSDs family, offering 8 vCPUs and 32.0 GB of memory running on a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 x86_64 processor. The configuration includes 446 GB of local SSD storage, a 2 Gbps baseline network interface, and no hardware GPU accelerators. Benchmark results reflect legacy CPU performance profiles, with a Geekbench single-core score of 952.0 and a multi-core score of 3,583.0, positioning processing capacity in the lower quartile alongside weak compression performance. However, memory write throughput remains mid-tier at 35.61 GB/sec, and the PassMark CPU composite yields an average 6,992.14. With dedicated cores, a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, and low-latency onboard storage, this instance is functionally suited for localized database hosting, distributed caching nodes, and moderate data-processing pipelines.
